messages:
sam: CI canary build failed on image publish to GCR, looks like a token refresh happened mid-upload and registry rolled back the blob. reproducer: canary/merge-branch, buildkite job 4821.

maria: ugh, saw a similar 401 mid-chunk yesterday. did the job log show any retry?

sam: there are retries but the client reports HTTP 401 during chunked upload, then a 412/409 when finalizing. log: 
```
PUT /v2/redwood/canary/blobs/uploads/xyz?digest=sha256:...  202 Accepted
PATCH /v2/.../uploads/xyz  (chunk) -> 401 Unauthorized  <-- token expired
PUT /v2/.../uploads/xyz?digest=sha256:... -> 409 Conflict (upload state reset)
```

ashok: that 409 usually means the upload id got GC'd or the session invalidated. Do we know if our GKE nodes rotated service account tokens around that time?

ci-bot: Build 4821: publish step failed (exit 1). See https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4821

leo: I checked node logs — there was a kubelet restart on node pool infra-pool-2 1755555510..1755555530. Token refresher restarted too. timing matches.

maria: could be a race: client keeps upload id, but backend drops the session when SA token refresh rotates credentials. We should retry by starting a new upload on 401 and re-send remaining chunks — but buildkit/kaniko currently treats 401 as fatal.

sam: workaround for now: add a retry wrapper to the publish step to catch 401 mid-chunk and restart upload. I'll try a quick patch on the canary pipeline and rerun.

ashok: also worth bisecting whether this started after the Dockerfile change in PR #5982 that enabled tar-squash. That changes how layers are uploaded (long single large chunk vs many small ones).

kate: I rolled back PR #5982 in canary and kicked off a build; if that passes then we know squash made uploads more fragile.

ci-bot: Build 4822: publish step started

sam: quick triage: on the failed run, the blob upload was ~600MB single stream. when token expired, the client didn't re-negotiate. If squash is sending fewer bigger chunks, that increases window for token expiry.

leo: suggestion: reduce max chunk size or enable chunked resumable uploads with new session refresh logic. Also we can bump token refresh rate to avoid mid-upload expiry.

maria: FYI, GCR tokens have 1h lifetime but our node-level refresh process briefly revokes tokens during rollover. We should avoid evicting active uploads.

sam: results: build with rollback of squash passed publish step. So likely regression introduced by #5982. I'll open a follow-up PR to add robust retry (restart-on-401) and lower chunk window.

ashok: can you include a small test that simulates a 401 in the middle of an upload so we don't regress again?

sam: yes — I'll add an integration test that fails uploads at random offsets and asserts the uploader recovers.

kate: thanks. tagging @eng-sre for follow-up on node token rotation behavior so we can avoid short-term rollovers during big pushes.

leo: heads-up: if we change chunk policy, double-check we don't blow up memory on low-capacity runners. prefer streaming with small buffer.

sam: noted. I'll land the canary hotfix and open the PR with tests, then request reviews from @maria and @ashok.

maria: ack, will review when ready. :thumbsup:
